retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version provena

nce, not historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-s
cope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts c

over only its requested
goal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather
than a fabricated map node.
The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open objects** on purpose.\nTheir upstream projections grow with the product a
nd the SDK types them the\nsame way, so pinning a field list would turn every new metric into a spec\nviolation. Read what you rec

ognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It st
ill draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the
window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is\n> why it is never inferred f

rom anything else.

**Feedback** — report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - |
- |\n| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summar
y, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-i
n accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated strictl
y — an empty or over-long key is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text goes to th

e MCPJam team, outside your organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint t
he `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one —\n> it lets the
team find that request in the server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` with the

original
> receipt instead of filing a second report.

**Planning** — one read that answers "may I?" before you try:

| En
dpoint | What it does |\n| - | - |\n| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, the beta gate's state, plan

limits, and the booleans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write still en
forces\n> independently, so a `true` here that races a flag flip costs you a clean\n> `403` rather than an incorrect success — and
nothing should consult it\n> *instead of* trying. It exists because agent surfaces are static: an MCP tool\n> catalog is built wi
th no organization in hand, so the alternative is\n> attempting the write and reading the failure, by which point the agent has\n>

usually already told someone what it was about to do.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](https://raw

.githubusercontent.com/MCPJam/inspector/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)
for Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.

## Se

rver accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-in, for e
xample because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nto a named

account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../a
ccounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\n| `GET
.../accounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replaces
its token in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: tr

ue`), or both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

```bash theme=
{\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/acco
unts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -d '
{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformation\": {

nnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an acco

unt

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account or answe
rs `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no account ha
s makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in

`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64 characte
rs. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are\nuniq

ue on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own l

abel, and
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
* **Uploaded accoun
ts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner
\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the proj
ect.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResou
rceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is at most 1
6 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or when t
he issuer rejects our refreshes, a\n stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an\n expired account l
ists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next\n upload restores it.\n* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and serv

er: 60, refilling at 120 an
 hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as t
he person who created it, with all of that person's\naccess. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who\
nis not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a\nserver shared with the project, accounts are project a

ccounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running eva

ls as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as one acco

unt, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATC
H \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorizat

ion: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes
the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which\nreads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and
\n`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the\n[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-

commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same time with differen
t defaults. Where your organization\nhas account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it\nruns as, in its

settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELET
E` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer\nto revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation
